module_title: MS PowerPoint - Slide Transitions and Custom Animations
introduction: This intermediate tier focuses on the most confusing and heavily tested topic in PowerPoint: distinguishing between 'Transitions' and 'Animations'. We will also cover specific slide show playback shortcuts.

core_concepts.title: Slide Transition
core_concepts.description: A visual effect that occurs when you move from ONE SLIDE to the NEXT SLIDE during a presentation. Examples include 'Fade', 'Wipe', or 'Push'. A transition is applied to the ENTIRE slide as a whole.

core_concepts.title: Animation
core_concepts.description: A visual effect applied to INDIVIDUAL OBJECTS (text, pictures, shapes) INSIDE a single slide. For example, making a bullet point fly in from the left, or making a picture spin. It is applied to elements, not the slide itself.

core_concepts.title: Custom Animation Types
core_concepts.description:
PowerPoint categorizes animations into four specific groups:
1. Entrance (How an object enters the screen).
2. Emphasis (Highlighting an object already on the screen).
3. Exit (How an object leaves the screen).
4. Motion Paths (Drawing a custom route for an object to move along).

core_concepts.title: Current Slide Show (Shift + F5)
core_concepts.description: If you are editing slide number 15 and want to test the slide show starting EXACTLY from slide 15 (without going back to slide 1), the shortcut is `Shift + F5`.

important_entities.name: Animation Pane
important_entities.significance: A side-panel that displays a sequential list of all animations applied to the current slide. It allows you to reorder, delay, or adjust the speed of individual effects.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners will test this concept explicitly. Rule of thumb: If the question mentions effects 'between slides' or 'moving from slide to slide', the answer is TRANSITION. If the question mentions effects on 'text, objects, or images', the answer is ANIMATION.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: T for Total (Transition), A for Assets (Animation)
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: A Transition affects the Total slide at once. An Animation affects the Assets (text, charts, images) inside it.

exam_strategy_tips: In SSC CGL, `Shift + F5` (Start Slide Show from Current Slide) is highly tested. Lock this in your memory alongside the standard `F5`.
